question: If I have attended 34 out of 50 classes (68% attendance), how many consecutive classes must I attend to reach 75%?
answer:
To reach the 75% cutoff, use the formula: classes_needed = ceil((0.75 * held - attended) / (1 - 0.75)).
With 50 classes held and 34 attended:
(0.75 * 50 - 34) / 0.25 = (37.5 - 34) / 0.25 = 3.5 / 0.25 = 14.
You must attend the next 14 consecutive classes without missing any class to reach exactly 75.0% (48 attended out of 64 total classes).
evidence_excerpt: Minimum 75% attendance calculation based on total conducted instructional hours.

question: Explain normalization in DBMS and describe 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, and BCNF.
answer:
Normalization in relational databases systematically decomposes tables to eliminate redundancy and prevent insertion, update, and deletion anomalies:
• 1NF: Atomic values only, no repeating groups.
• 2NF: In 1NF and no partial dependencies on composite keys.
• 3NF: In 2NF and no transitive dependencies.
• BCNF: Strict 3NF where every determinant is a candidate key.
evidence_excerpt: Database normalization reduces redundancy through progressive normal forms.

question: What is the difference between Quicksort and Mergesort in algorithmic complexity?
answer: Quicksort has average time complexity O(n log n) and in-place space complexity O(log n), but worst-case O(n^2) on poor pivot selection. Mergesort provides a guaranteed O(n log n) time across all cases and is stable, but requires auxiliary O(n) memory.
evidence_excerpt: Quicksort is in-place with O(n log n) average; Mergesort is stable with O(n) space.
